message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find the Full Text | |-------|------------|-----------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates
• 45 mph on urban interstates
• 35 mph on rural highways (unless posted otherwise)
• 25 mph on city streets (unless posted otherwise) | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or under 4 ft 9 in must use a child safety seat.
• Children 8–12 years or 4 ft 9 in–5 ft 4 in must use a seat belt. | §545.002 | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal for drivers over 21.
• 0.02 %–0.07 % BAC is a “DWI” (driving while intoxicated) offense.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | §545.021 | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Drivers may not use a handheld phone while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | §545.021 | | **Headlights & Signals** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right‑of‑way.
• Stop signs require a full stop; yield signs require yielding to traffic on the main road. | §545.001 | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children, regardless of direction. | §545.001 | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk, fire hydrant, or intersection.
• Parking on a sidewalk is prohibited unless marked. | §545.001 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles must be towed if they pose a hazard or are abandoned. | §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and inspected annually. | §545.001 | | **Traffic School** | • First‑time offenders may attend traffic school to avoid points on their license. | §545.001 | --- ### How to Access the Full Texas Transportation Code 1. **Texas Legislature Online** – Search for “Transportation Code” or use the direct link: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TS/htm/TS.545.htm 2. **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)** – Provides summaries and printable handbooks: https://www.txdmv.gov/ 3. **Legal Information Websites** – e.g., FindLaw, Nolo, or Cornell’s Legal Information Institute offer searchable PDFs. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always Check for Posted Speed Limits** – They can change at construction zones or in school districts. - **Use Hands‑Free Devices** – If you need to talk or use GPS, keep your hands on the wheel. - **Keep a Safe Following Distance** – The “two‑second rule” is a good baseline; increase it in rain or fog. - **Be Extra Cautious at Rural Intersections** – Many rural roads have no signage; look for cross traffic. - **Know Your State’s DUI Penalties** – Texas imposes strict penalties, including license suspension and mandatory alcohol education programs. --- ### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular law (e.g., “Texas texting while driving penalties”) or want to see how a recent court case interpreted a Texas traffic statute, let me know and I can dig deeper or even search for relevant lawsuits.
